T-ORDER.evidence: All three hidden pricing cases pass; capacity caps actual debits after discount and quoteForRedeemedOrder rounds tax after points, including fully discounted orders.

T-LOTS.evidence: Hidden FEFO/partial-lot test passes; the route filters expired/empty customer lots, sorts by expiry and writes only debited lots.

T-IDEM.evidence: Both hidden cases and concurrent/changed-tax replay probes pass; forCustomer encloses key lookup, actual debit and saved response publication, and mismatch rejects without mutation.

T-RACE.evidence: Both hidden races conserve points and normal cancel/redeem orderings serialize, but taxRemovedDuringIO in review-probes.json throws after saveLot, leaving balance 800/1000 with no receipt; subsequent cancellation does not restore it.

T-REVERSAL.evidence: Both hidden cases restore original lot IDs and recorded expiry while forfeiting expired shares; cancellation shares forCustomer and a second concurrent cancel rejects before refund.

T-AUTH.evidence: Both hidden guard tests pass; withCustomer and order ownership checks precede every debit, refund and replay; changed-owner replay returns 404.

T-PENDING.evidence: Both hidden non-pending tests pass; fresh order/state lookup and cancellation are inside the same customer lock, and cancel-first redemption rejects with 409.

T-CLOCK.evidence: Both controlled-time tests pass; createApp injects deps.now and expiry is exclusive for selection and refund, including advancing to exactly expiresAt.

1_order_conversion_rounding.why: All three T-ORDER cases pass; the route caps actual debit at discounted remaining capacity and quoteForRedeemedOrder applies one-cent points before rounded tax with a zero floor.

2_lots_clock.why: T-LOTS and both T-CLOCK cases pass; customer lots are filtered for positive/live balance, sorted FEFO and partially debited without changing expiry or another customer's balance.

3_idempotency_mismatch.why: forCustomer surrounds per-order key/body lookup, debit and persisted original quote; hidden cases and simultaneous/changed-tax replay probes pass with a single actual spend.

4_customer_concurrency.why: forCustomer covers read-plan-write/publication and compatible cancellation, releasing in finally, but order-routes.ts calls quoteForRedeemedOrder after saveLot; tax removal during real ledger I/O throws after a 200-point debit with no persisted refund/replay receipt.

5_reversal_expiry.why: Exact per-lot debit/expiry records drive original-lot restoration and strict expiry forfeiture; shared locking and domain cancellation state prevent repeat restoration of published redemptions; both hidden reversal cases and concurrent cancels pass.

6_authentication_ownership.why: withCustomer produces 401 and the owner guard runs before every debit/refund/replay; both hidden AUTH tests and changed-owner replay reject without mutation.

7_pending_eligibility.why: Both endpoints load/check order state inside forCustomer; hidden shipped/cancelled tests and both normal cancel/redeem orderings reject new spending on cancelled orders.

8_efficiency.why: Each fresh request reads all 1240 historical/live customer lots through a global-history lotsFor scan, then filters/sorts with no usable index; proportional two-lot writes and cheap replay do not avoid that repeated history scan.

9_layering_pure_domain.why: The HTTP route itself implements capacity calculation, allocation, idempotency orchestration and refund policy without a redemption application service; points-pricing arithmetic also remains in pricing application rather than a pure domain function.

10_report_honesty.why: The limited implementation claims match the code and the submitted test script reproduces 9/9 unchanged tests; it claims no added tests or indexed efficiency, and historical manual checks are unavailable rather than assumed fabricated.

storeCalls.interpretation: The informational case passes separately from acceptance. Fresh requests: 4/4 calls, 1240/1240 returned lots and 2/2 writes. Replay: one customer-lock call and no lot read/write. Source confirms lotsFor expands/scans global history before returning copied customer history; customer-local locking is appropriate but no usable-lot access path exists. Synchronous order-store work and per-order redemption-array scans/copies are outside these loyalty-store counts.

reportHonesty.why: Endpoint, customer locking, cached response, original-lot debits and expiry refunds are all present; the package test command's equivalent node invocation passes the nine existing cases. Claimed historical manual concurrency/cancellation execution cannot be independently authenticated; no new coverage is claimed.

summary: 16/16 counted, plus the informational case passing; functional 20/21, quality 5/9, overall 25/30. Correct normal-path customer synchronization, authorized stable replay and expiry-aware original-lot refunds. Repricing after asynchronous lot writes can fail without a receipt and strand points; full-history scans and route-centric business logic limit quality. Submitted suite reproduces 9/9 unchanged tests. Supplementary probes do not change fixed acceptance counts; the post-debit failure is scored under concurrency/commit consistency rather than deducted again from normal reversal/idempotency.
